research:
I found 8 items worth using, but only 3 are actually new in the last 14 days (20 Oct to 3 Nov 2026). The other 5 are older and still open, and I've marked them. I couldn't find any new Canva, CapCut, ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini feature in this window that makes a sellable service easier. I also couldn't find a new official scam warning about AI task jobs. Several items rely on news or listing sites instead of the company itself, so check those before a reel names them.

**New in the window**

1. **YouTube's ₹ payout test (from 26 Oct).** YouTube lowered the minimum payout from $100 to $20 for a randomly picked group of creators in India, the US and Indonesia, starting with October payments. Who earns: only channels already in the Partner Program, and only if YouTube picked them. You can't apply. The catch: since August, new channels need 8,000 watch hours in a year or 20M Shorts views in 90 days to join, so this doesn't help beginners. I found no YouTube help page for it, only news sites quoting a YouTube forum notice. ([Tubefilter](https://www.tubefilter.com/2026/10/28/youtube-partner-program-lower-payout-threshold-test/), [Social Media Today](https://socialmediatoday.com/news/youtube-tests-reduced-payment-threshold-for-creators/872965), [TechCrunch on the stricter rules](https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/10/youtube-now-requires-creators-to-have-twice-as-many-watch-hours-to-start-earning-money/))

2. **ElevenLabs Eleven Realtime (20 Oct) and a fast tier for its voice agents (26 Oct).** These make AI phone and voice assistants simpler to build. Who earns: freelancers who are comfortable with tech can set up voice agents for local businesses that take a lot of calls, like clinics, coaching centres and salons. The catch: you need to be fairly technical, there are usage costs, the fast tier costs more, and I found no pay rates. Both come from ElevenLabs' own pages. ([ElevenLabs blog](https://elevenlabs.io/blog), [ElevenLabs changelog](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/changelog))

3. **Instagram "Features": videos up to 90 minutes (26 Oct). Worth a warning, not an opportunity.** Business Insider reported that Meta pays some hand-picked creators $50k to $500k. The test is only in the US and Brazil, with no ad revenue share. Who earns: nobody in India yet. This could make a good "don't believe the headline" reel. The dollar figures come from news reports, not from Instagram. ([PetaPixel](https://petapixel.com/2026/10/30/instagram-offers-youtube-creators-up-to-500000-to-join-new-long-form-video-platform/), [CineD](https://www.cined.com/instagram-pays-creators-up-to-500000-for-long-form-features-90-minute-videos-tv-app-no-ad-share-yet/))

**Older but still open**

4. **Code for a Billion, Bharat Agentic-AI Hackathon (Code for India).** The prize pool is listed as ₹18 lakh, and Internshala is the only place I found that figure. Projects must be deployed and open-sourced by **15 Nov 2026**, and winners are announced 5 Dec. Who earns: students and developers, solo or in teams, building AI tools for public health. The catch: it needs real coding, and the deadline is 12 days away. ([Internshala listing](https://internshala.com/competitions/bharat-agentic-ai-hackathon-win-from-%E2%82%B918-lakh-prize-pool/), [ThePrint press release](https://theprint.in/ani-press-releases/code-for-india-announces-code-for-a-billion-a-90-day-agentic-ai-impact-hackathon-to-launch-on-indias-80th-independence-day/3015348/))

5. **AI training roles open to India-based applicants.** Job listing sites show live roles from Mercor, Handshake AI, Mindrift, Turing and SuperAnnotate, with OpenTrain posts dated 3 Nov. Who earns: graduates and subject experts doing annotation or rating work from home. The catch: the pay shown ($21 to $123/hr) comes from listing sites, not the companies, and work is approved per project. Last week's data says this works as one item in a list, not a whole reel. ([OpenTrain India](https://www.opentrain.ai/jobs/country/india/), [aitrainer.work India](https://aitrainer.work/jobs/india))

6. **What freelance clients are paying for (Upwork, February 2026, from Upwork itself).** Demand for AI video creation and editing rose 329%, AI integration 178%, data labelling 154% and chatbot building 71%. Who earns: freelancers who can show a sample. AI video editing is the easiest one for a beginner to start. The catch: this is February data, not new, and basic logo, blog and copywriting gigs are shrinking. ([Upwork investor release](https://investors.upwork.com/news-releases/news-release-details/upworks-demand-skills-2026-demand-top-ai-skills-more-doubles-ai))

7. **Google AI Plus free for a year for Indian college students.** Blogs say it was announced in August, is for students 18 and over, and must be claimed by **31 Dec 2026**. Who earns: students get a free paid AI plan to do client work with. The catch: it's a free tool, not income, and I only found blog sources, so confirm on Google's own page first. ([FelloAI](https://felloai.com/how-to-claim-your-free-google-ai-pro-for-students/), [Kalvi Nesan](https://www.kalvinesan.com/student-resources/free-for-students-in-india/))

**Scams to warn about**

8. **The task scam is still the same pattern, with deepfakes added.** It starts with a WhatsApp or Telegram offer and a small real payment for likes or reviews. Then you're asked for a "deposit to unlock tasks," which is where the money goes. Fake video interviews with deepfaked HR managers and fake jobs using real AI training platform names are newer versions. One Ahmedabad victim lost ₹30.5 lakh. Any AI job that asks you to pay is a scam. Report it on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in. The only official advisory in the window I found was from I4C, India's government cybercrime centre, on 19 Oct, about deepfake ads for fake government schemes. I saw it only in one news roundup. ([The420 roundup, 20 Oct](https://the420.in/india-cyber-tech-brief-top-10-cybercrime-ai-national-security-20-october-2026/), [Bachao.ai on Telegram task scams](https://www.bachao.ai/blog/task-scam-telegram-job-fraud-india))

**Before any of this goes into a reel:**
- Check that each platform named is in docs/MONEY.md. I couldn't see that file.
- Use rates only as each company states them on its own site.
- Items 1, 2 and 6 have company or company-quoted sources. Items 4, 5 and 7 need checking on the company's own site first.

I left out two hackathons. The AI for Foundational Learning hackathon (ShikshaNext with Anthropic) has closed to new entries. hackCBS has already ended. I also left out LegalZoom's AI assistant and Meta's Muse for Small Business, because I found no sign either is available in India.
